service.description: What needs an administrator on this instance, as one list (plans/archive/Tools-Fancy.md §3.4). Each item is {key, severity (critical, warning or info), text, count, value, link, parameters}: count for an item that counts records (at most 100: a count of 100 is "100 or more"), value for a resource reading (its percent), link a route under /apps with its parameters. The resource readings whose level is not ok come first (the status map's Resources: disk space and inodes of each filesystem, memory, CPU load, open files, the certificates the HTTPS listener serves, swap), the most severe first; then the listeners and integrations that failed or were skipped, a draining instance, saturated workers or database pool, the readiness checks that are not ready, system messages in error, open incidents, firing alerts, failing checks and scrape targets, new error groups and agent approvals waiting. The readiness checks are those of org.moqui.admin.ReadinessServices.get#Readiness, the one source Health reads too, asked for the instance's own (a provider whose registration names a scope, such as an organization, is left to Health): the framework's own (no outgoing mail server, a paused or unmirrored backup, report delivery, an administrator without a second factor, failed job runs of the last day, a silent cluster member, lost or unknown telemetry, a failing protocol, Constitution sources passed over) and each component's registered provider, as the user may read them; a failed check is critical, a warning or unavailable one a warning, its key the check's and its link its fix place where that is a System screen; the ten worst are listed and the rest counted with a link to Health. Each item is checked on its own: one that fails is logged as an error and left out, and the others still come back. An item whose source the user may not read (the entity, the dataset, the service, a provider's permission, or MONITOR_INCIDENT for incidents) is left out; it reads nothing but counts and the checks' own answers. Refuses nothing.

parameter.name: items
parameter.description: The items, resource readings first, then the most severe first

service.description: The recent history of the System home's counters, for their sparklines: for each of load, memory, disk, workers and pool the values of its gauge over the period (from, such as now-1h), one a bucket of the range, oldest first, null where there is none; disk is the fullest filesystem's in each bucket. Read from the otel_metrics dataset through the report engine as the user, narrowed to instanceId when one is given. A series that cannot be read (telemetry off, the dataset not the user's to read, a query that fails) is logged, when it is a failure, and left out; the others still come back. Refuses nothing.

parameter.name: series
parameter.description: load, memory, disk, workers, pool: each a list of numbers
